\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas.QBFEncoding}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean Encoding of Quantifiers]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.quantBit}
\label{Complexity.QBF.quantBit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
The Boolean encoding of a quantifier is true for an existential quantifier and false for
a universal quantifier.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quantifier from a Boolean]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit}
\label{Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
Associate the existential quantifier to true and the universal quantifier to false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoding a Quantified Boolean Formula]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.encode}
\label{Complexity.QBF.encode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF, Complexity.QBF.quantBit, Std.Sat.CNF.serialize, Turing.pairEncode}
A quantified Boolean formula consists of a finite list of quantifiers and a CNF matrix
over variables indexed by the natural numbers. Its encoding is the pairing encoding of
the list obtained by replacing each quantifier by its Boolean encoding and the
serialization of its CNF matrix.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decoding a Quantified Boolean Formula]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.decode}
\label{Complexity.QBF.decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF, Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit, Std.Sat.CNF.decode, Std.Sat.CNF.fallback, Turing.pairDecode}
For a Boolean string, first attempt to decode it as a pair consisting of a
quantifier-bit list and a CNF-matrix encoding. If this succeeds, replace each quantifier
bit by its corresponding quantifier and decode the matrix; if it fails, return the
formula with an empty quantifier list and the fallback CNF matrix.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quantifier Bit Round Trip]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit_quantBit}
\label{Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit_quantBit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant, Complexity.QBF.quantBit, Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit}
\difficulty{4}
For either Boolean quantifier, encoding it as a bit and then interpreting that bit as a
quantifier returns the original quantifier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decoding an Encoded Quantified Formula]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.decode_encode}
\label{Complexity.QBF.decode_encode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF, Complexity.QBF.decode, Complexity.QBF.encode, Complexity.QBF.quantOfBit_quantBit, Std.Sat.CNF.decode_serialize, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
For every quantified Boolean formula $Q$, decoding its encoding recovers $Q$ exactly:
the quantifier prefix and the CNF matrix are both unchanged.
\end{theorem}
